episode.episode: Philips Hue: The smart home’s light bulb moment
episode.showDescription: Version History is a show about the best gadgets ever. And the worst ones. And the ones that might have changed the world, if they ever actually shipped. Every week, your favorite people from The Verge and beyond hang out to tell and debate the story of a gadget, app, website, or any other tech product, and try to determine the item’s true legacy. Because not every product is a hit, but every product has a story. And the ones that really matter aren’t always the ones you think. From the Verge and the Vox Media Podcast Network.
episode.episodeDescription: The humble light bulb might be the ultimate success story in the smart home. Our connected, adaptable homes are supposed to be customizable, connected to everything, and incredibly easy to use, and nothing has made that work quite like Philips Hue lights. In this episode, The Verge's David Pierce and Jennifer Pattison Tuohy are joined by smart home journalist and expert Richard Gunther to tell the Hue's story. We trace the product's history from its origins in the smartphone revolution, try to figure out how Philips managed to turn a staggeringly expensive lightbulb into a must-have gadget, and look at whether there's even more invention left in the future of lighting. We’re also on video! Check us out on YouTube. Subscribe to The Verge for unlimited access to theverge.com, subscriber-exclusive newsletters, and our ad-free podcast feed. We love hearing from you! Email your questions and thoughts to vergecast@theverge.com or call us at 866-VERGE11. Learn more about your ad choices. Visit podcastchoices.com/adchoices

transcript_window.text: It's much more the tones.
The temperature is more important for me.
But it is fun, you know, around holidays and such.
But I think it was peak color changing lighting, maybe.
I don't know.
Richard, do you have any wacky scenes?
What makes your lights flash?
I don't have any wacky scenes, actually, except I like using them for for fun stuff at Halloween and stuff like that.
There's some really great apps that allow you to play scary effects that sync with lights to make it look like, you know, dungeon lighting or things like that.
So that can be kind of fun.
Yeah, that's pretty good.
No, for me, I mean, it's always been about the ambiance for me.

And, you know, we didn't even get to talk about the product that Jen talked me into buying, which was the Hue Sync, which allows the Hue Sync box, which will synchronize what's going on with your TV, with the room.
Right.
I mean, stuff like that.
I kind of feel like they've done better than anybody else in terms of creating experiences with light.
So maybe peak lighting experience.
I like that.
What I do think they have in terms of peakness is peak integration.
I don't think anybody has done it as well as they have.
And it's not just their lighting products.

Their lighting products, their sensors, and by the way, they make amongst the best sensors on the market, and their buttons and remotes, it's all accessible through all these other ecosystems, which is smart, smart, smart.
Yeah, that's really good.
Good.
And I remember, especially in those early days when Alexa, Google Assistant, and then HomeKit were all really on the come up.
They were all so different that I feel like I spent a lot of my time, and I'm sure you both spent a lot of your time, just explaining to people what worked with what.
